official.description_text:
Postdoc in Experimental Oncology
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will work on functional and molecular studies of nuclear receptors in various models, as well as on bioinformatics. The project aims to understand the relationship between estrogen signaling, tumor development, and the intestinal microenvironment. You are expected to plan and conduct experiments, analyze and interpret complex datasets, present results at research meetings and international conferences, write scientific papers, and contribute to research grant applications. The work will be carried out within the Experimental Oncology research group at KTH and includes some supervision of doctoral and master’s students.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made
Extensive research expertise in molecular biology, hormone signaling, and cancer research
Documented ability to conduct research, demonstrated through high-quality scientific publications
FELASA certification and prior experience with mouse models
Strong communication skills, both orally and in writing
Good organizational skills
Proficiency in English, as this is required for daily work
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Previous experience with cell culture, analysis of clinical samples, RNA-seq, and bioinformatics
Research experience in biological sex differences, as well as estrogen and inflammatory signaling
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively
Experience in supervision
Knowledge of diversity and equal treatment issues, with a particular focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A
position as a postdoctoral fellow
is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in experimental oncology at KTH Stockholm, focused on molecular and functional studies of nuclear receptors, estrogen signaling, and tumor development using mouse models, cell culture, and bioinformatics.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is biomedical research (cancer biology, hormone signaling, molecular mechanisms). Researcher's domain is human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, and collaborative learning. These operate in entirely different research paradigms.

methodological_fit.rationale: Limited methodological connection. Both involve experimental design and data interpretation. Researcher has intermediate experimental-design skills from user studies. However, oncology work requires wet-lab protocols (FELAS certification, mouse models, cell culture, RNA-seq), molecular biology expertise, and statistical analysis (mixed-effects modelling required but researcher has none). The experimental frameworks are incompatible.

growth_value.rationale: No growth value. Oncology research contributes nothing to human-centred XR, spatial cognition, collaborative immersive systems, or HCI methodology. Would not close any capability gaps relevant to target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH Stockholm is in Sweden (preferred country), providing geographic fit. However, the research community in experimental oncology is entirely disconnected from HCI, XR, or the researcher's target trajectory. This is a pure biomedical position with no strategic value for building toward the stated target identity.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress); position requires PhD. Not currently eligible unless degree is completed and conferred before employment decision.
FELAS certification required; researcher has none and would need to obtain it.
Extensive molecular biology and cancer research expertise required; researcher has none.
Preferred: PhD within last 3 years; researcher has not completed PhD.
risks: PhD eligibility gap: researcher must complete degree before appointment.
Severe expertise gap: position requires FELAS certification, mouse model expertise, molecular biology proficiency, and cancer research background. Researcher has none of these.
Research community disconnect: oncology group at KTH has no connection to HCI, XR, or immersive systems research.
Career trajectory risk: 2-year biomedical postdoc would significantly complicate applications to HCI-focused PhD or research positions.
High failure risk: researcher would enter a domain where they lack foundational wet-lab training, certification, and disciplinary background.
Supervision expectation: position involves supervising PhD and MSc students in oncology; researcher lacks both discipline knowledge and supervisory experience in this field.
